title: Throughput guarantee framework: surge windows, autoscale interlock, and contract wording
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a pragmatic, contract-safe SLA for dedicated throughput that supports short burst behavior (surge windows), ties into autoscaler behavior (autoscale interlock), and produces unambiguous credit computation language for contracts and invoices.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 3-tier measurement model: steady-state entitlement (committed TPM), surge allowance (short-window multiplier), and error-budgeted overage credits. Autoscale will be permitted to burst beyond committed throughput up to the surge allowance for configured windows; however, when error budget consumption exceeds thresholds we'll interlock autoscale and require shedding or fallback to lower-cost variants. Contracts will reference quantile-based measurement windows and a deterministic credit formula (token-seconds deficit) to compute customer credits.
measurement_spec: SLO target: Committed Throughput = X tokens-per-minute (tpm) averaged over 10m sliding windows. Surge Window = configurable N seconds (default 60s) where provider allows burst up to Mx the committed tpm (default M=3). Degradation is measured using a 95th percentile of per-minute served tokens over billing hour and a rolling 30-day quantile for chronic degradations. Error budget consumption is computed as (Committed tpm - Observed tpm)_positive integrated over the billing period as token-seconds; credits convert token-seconds into % monthly bill by a pre-agreed rate. Monitoring: metrics exported to console: committed_tpm, observed_tpm, surge_events_count, token_seconds_deficit, cumulative_credit_balance.
contract_language_snippet: SLA: Redwood guarantees that dedicated capacity customers will receive the Committed Throughput (as specified in the Order) measured as the average tokens-per-minute over rolling 10-minute windows. Redwood permits short-duration bursts up to the Surge Multiplier (M) for Surge Windows (default 60s). In the event Observed Throughput falls below Committed Throughput for durations beyond allowable surge rules, Customer is eligible for Service Credits. Service Credits are calculated by converting the cumulative token deficit (token-seconds) during the Measurement Period into a percentage of the Monthly Fee using the Credit Rate table attached as Exhibit A. Credits are subject to the Customer providing notice within 30 days of event discovery. Scheduled maintenance, customer-caused traffic patterns, and Force Majeure are excluded. Redwood's remedies are limited to Service Credits; other remedies are expressly disclaimed. For chronic underperformance, Redwood will engage the customer and propose remediation including autoscale adjustments, model variant fallbacks, or pro-rated refunds as outlined in the Deductible Remediation Ladder.
acceptance_criteria: Legal approves SLA and Credit Rate exhibit
Instrumentation exports required metrics and uses existing telemetry schema
Billing integration computes token-seconds deficits and posts credits to customer billing account in test environment
Console shows realtime surge allowance, current credit balance, and projected credit impact for visible events
E2E test harness can simulate bursts and verify credit calculation against golden model
rollout_plan: Draft SLA and Credit Exhibit -> Legal review (week 1)
Implement telemetry and billing compute in staging (week 1-2)
Open canary with 3 pilot customers on offered terms (week 3)
Collect telemetry, run audit, finalize contract templates (week 4)
Flip to GA and publish docs + console UI (week 5)

2026-03-06: PM/Legal synced on consumer-friendly wording that avoids open-ended penalty exposure. Legal requested a 30-day notice requirement and an Exhibit for rates.
2026-03-08: Draft billing job implemented in staging; credit calculation matches golden script on synthetic traces (within rounding error).
2026-03-10: PR opened for console UI card showing Surge Allowance and Credit Balance. Waiting for design review and UX copy updates.
review_feedback: Design (Linda Cho) 2026-03-09: UI should show both remaining surge quota for the current window and historical surge events in the last 24h.
